title: Medical biochemistry and nutrition
audience: a medical student in the preclinical years
purpose: Explain vitamins and minerals, inherited disorders of carbohydrate, lipid, amino acid, purine and heme metabolism, lysosomal and connective-tissue disorders, nutrition, malnutrition and the biochemistry of obesity and diabetes.

weeks.12: Biochemistry of obesity, diabetes and metabolic syndrome

blocks.deliverable: Match vitamin deficiencies to their clinical findings.
Explain hypoglycemia in von Gierke disease.
Compare the familial dyslipidemias by defect and labs.
Week 7 midterm; explain phenylketonuria and its newborn screen.
Explain the findings in lead poisoning and acute intermittent porphyria.
Submit the project; take an unseen 150 minute final in week 14.

project: Metabolic disease casebook: write six short cases that link a defective enzyme to its laboratory findings, presentation and treatment.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
